newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Central America to tackle growing AIDS problem.
newsitem.headline: Central America to tackle growing AIDS problem.

text.p: Central American legislators and health experts will meet in Nicaragua next week to discuss the region's growing AIDS problem, the Nicaraguan government said on Thursday.
In the first meeting of its kind, 30 to 35 Central American lawmakers will meet with directors of the region's anti-AIDS programmes, a government press release said.
The meeting, next Monday and Tuesday, is being organised by the New York-based Interamerican Parliamentary Group.
Its objectives are to educate regional legislators about AIDS and the HIV virus, coordinate parliamentary action and promote changes to AIDS-related legislation, it said.

The Panamerican Health Organisation has reported 11,142 AIDS cases in Central America, a rate of 52 cases per million people, but estimated the number of reported cases was only 10 percent of the total, the press release said.
"With the passage of time the epidemiological profile of AIDS in our societies is changing, with an ever greater number of women with the virus," it said.
El Salvador has about 1,600 reported cases of AIDS, Guatemala 1,300, Costa Rica 1,012, Panama 1,186, Nicaragua 284 and Belize 138, Nicaragua's health ministry said. It had no figure for Honduras.
